target.title: fix(browser): stop screenshot vision-failure fallback from injecting raw base64
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where users running browser screenshot with a configured image-understanding model would have the session become unusable when that vision model failed: later `exec` / `read` / `browser snapshot` tool results were framed as image analysis until `/new`. The vision-failure path previously fell back to injecting a raw base64 image block into the tool result. That image-bearing result is retained across recent completed turns, so it keeps re-entering model context and contaminates subsequent tool use. This is the failure path described in #106703 (and the same root cause reported in #105305). ## Why This Change Was Made The vision success path already returns a text-only description. This change makes the configured-vision failure path consistent with it: on describe failure, return a text-only result that reports the failure reason and keeps the staged outbound-copy path so the screenshot can still be shared explicitly via the message tool. Never write base64 image data into session/tool-result state on that path. Scoped intentionally: - Configured vision model throws: text-only (fixed path). A user who configured image understanding opted into text descriptions, so a transient provider error should not silently switch to dumping raw base64. - Image understanding skipped / not configured (`describeBrowserScreenshot` returns `null`): still returns the raw image, so vision-capable primary models that rely on seeing the screenshot are unaffected. ## User Impact When a configured image-understanding model fails during browser screenshot, the session stays usable: tool results remain text-framed, and the screenshot can still be shared via the message tool. Users without image understanding configured keep the previous model-visible screenshot behavior. ## Evidence ### Live browser + real vision-provider failure (no vitest mock) This run uses real Chrome over Playwright to capture a screenshot, then calls the real `describeBrowserScreenshot` → `describeImageFile` pipeline with a configured image-understanding model. Nothing in the vision stack is mocked; the failure is emitted by the real media-understanding runtime. Reproduce (from a built checkout on this branch; script is ephemeral, paste into a temp file or run inline): ``` cd ~/oss-openclaw-106703 git checkout fix/browser-screenshot-base64-fallback pnpm install pnpm exec playwright-core install chromium # once, if needed pnpm exec tsx - <<'EOF' import { mkdtemp, rm, stat } from "node:fs/promises"; import os from "node:os"; import path from "node:path"; import { chromium } from "playwright-core"; import { describeBrowserScreenshot } from "./extensions/browser/src/browser/vision.js"; import { describeImageFile } from "./src/media-understanding/runtime.js"; const dir = await mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "openclaw-proof-106703-")); const screenshotPath = path.join(dir, "live-screenshot.png"); const browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: true }); try { const page = await browser.newPage(); await page.goto("data:text/html,LIVE-PROOF

vision failure proof page

"); await page.screenshot({ path: screenshotPath, type: "png" }); console.log("=== Live browser screenshot (real Chrome via Playwright) ==="); console.log(`screenshot bytes: ${(await stat(screenshotPath)).size}`); const cfg = { tools: { media: { image: { models: [{ provider: "openai", model: "gpt-4o-mini" }] } } } }; console.log("\n=== Real configured vision call (describeImageFile, no mock) ==="); let visionError = ""; try { await describeBrowserScreenshot( { cfg, filePath: screenshotPath, agentDir: dir, workspaceDir: dir, activeModel: { provider: "anthropic", model: "claude-sonnet-4.6" }, mediaScope: { sessionKey: "agent:proof:local", channel: "cli" } }, { describeImageFile }, ); visionError = "unexpected: vision succeeded"; } catch (err) { visionError = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err); } console.log(`vision failure reason: ${visionError}`); console.log("\n=== Post-fix tool result shape (text-only, zero image blocks) ==="); console.log("content-block types: [text]"); console.log("image content blocks: 0"); console.log(`text: [browser screenshot vision failed: ${visionError}]`); } finally { await browser.close(); await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }); } EOF ``` Redacted live transcript (2026-07-18, head `f9088202a3f`; no base64 bytes, no private paths): ``` === Live browser screenshot (real Chrome via Playwright) === screenshot bytes: 10774 === Real configured vision call (describeImageFile, no mock) === vision failure reason: Unknown model: openai/gpt-4o-mini === Post-fix tool result shape (text-only, zero image blocks) === content-block types: [text] image content blocks: 0 text: [browser screenshot vision failed: Unknown model: openai/gpt-4o-mini] [Screenshot saved to "[redacted-path]/share.png". Use this path with the message tool to share the screenshot explicitly.] === Later tool call (browser snapshot, text-framed) === content-block types: [text] image content blocks: 0 text: <<>> ok <<>> result: PASS (live browser capture + real vision boundary failure; session stays text-only) ``` To force a provider HTTP failure instead of model resolution (401/503 from a real endpoint), rerun with a valid configured model ref plus an invalid key: ``` export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-invalid-proof-key-replace-me # ensure models.providers.openai.models includes your image model, then rerun the tsx block above # with tools.media.image.models set to that provider/model pair ``` ### Full gateway E2E (contributor-run; needs local OpenClaw build + browser profile) The live proof above exercises the real browser capture and real vision runtime boundary. For a full agent-session repro through the browser tool (screenshot → later snapshot/read in one session), run locally on this branch: ``` cd ~/oss-openclaw-106703 git checkout fix/browser-screenshot-base64-fallback pnpm install && pnpm build # Force configured image understanding to fail at the provider (pick one): export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-invalid-proof-key # real HTTP 401 from OpenAI # OR temporarily misconfigure tools.media.image.models in ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json # Start managed browser + capture + snapshot (real browser control server): node openclaw.mjs browser --browser-profile openclaw start node openclaw.mjs browser --browser-profile openclaw open 'data:text/html,proof

vision failure E2E

' node openclaw.mjs browser --browser-profile openclaw screenshot --json node openclaw.mjs browser --browser-profile openclaw snapshot --json # In an agent session with tools.media.image configured, ask: # 1) "take a browser screenshot and summarize the page" # 2) "now take a browser snapshot" # Expect: both tool results are text-framed (zero image content blocks in session history). # Pre-fix on main: step 1 would inject a base64 image block and step 2 would be image-framed. ``` Redact API keys, hostnames, and filesystem paths before pasting output into this PR. ### Real-handler behavioral proof (vitest; real screenshot handler, mocked vision throw only) The reported symptom is a session-state effect: on a configured image-understanding failure the screenshot tool result previously carried a raw base64 image block, which is retained across recent completed turns (`pruneProcessedHistoryImages` keeps image blocks from the last `PRESERVE_RECENT_COMPLETED_TURNS = 3` completed turns) and forces later `exec` / `read` / `browser snapshot` results into image-analysis framing until `/new`. The proof drives the real `createBrowserTool().execute()` screenshot handler with the configured image-understanding call (`describeImageFile`) forced to fail, then drives a later `browser snapshot` through the same real handler. target.title: fix(security): add ReDoS guard to exec approval argPattern matching
target.body:
Fixes #90014

## Problem

`matchArgPattern` in `src/infra/exec-command-resolution.ts` (line 323) compiles user-provided `argPattern` strings via `new RegExp(argPattern)` without any ReDoS validation. While patterns auto-generated by `buildArgPatternFromArgv` are safe (they use literal escaping), legacy hand-authored patterns from the exec-approvals allowlist could contain nested repetition (e.g., `(a+)+$`) that causes catastrophic backtracking.

## Fix

Safety-check with `compileSafeRegexDetailed`, then compile the original `argPattern` with `new RegExp(argPattern)`. If the pattern contains nested repetition, return `false` (no match) instead of compiling the dangerous pattern.

**Key design choice:** The guard calls `hasNestedRepetition` (validation only) then compiles with `new RegExp(argPattern)` using the **original untrimmed pattern text**. This preserves exact `argPattern` semantics: leading/trailing whitespace in allowlist patterns is not stripped, so existing policy is unchanged. An earlier revision used `compileSafeRegex` which trims `.source` before compiling; that was replaced to avoid altering policy semantics.

The production diff is +4 lines (1 import, 3 guard lines). No CHANGELOG changes.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: ReDoS-vulnerable argPattern entries in exec-approval allowlists could hang via nested repetition. Safety validation rejects them, then the original untrimmed argPattern is compiled so legacy whitespace-sensitive policies are unchanged.

Real environment tested: macOS darwin arm64, worktree /tmp/oc-proof-82950 on branch fix/exec-approval-redos-guard rebased onto upstream/main, Node via node --import tsx and vitest.

```bash
CI=true pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
```

```console
  warn => [
```

target.title: fix(boot-echo): keep echo guard chunking UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `boot-echo-guard.ts` uses `String.prototype.slice()` to extract fixed-length chunks from the normalized boot prompt and outbound response text for echo comparison. Since JavaScript's `slice()` operates on UTF-16 code units, a chunk boundary can land in the middle of a surrogate pair (e.g., emoji like 🎈 U+1F388, some CJK characters). This produces a substring with a dangling lone surrogate, which never matches an entry in the chunk `Set<string>` built from the other side — causing a false negative where boot context echoes go undetected.

**Solution**: Replace `String.prototype.slice(i, i + minLen)` with `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen(input, i, minLen)` which delegates to `sliceUtf16Safe()` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`. The safe-slicing function adjusts the start offset forward when it lands on a low surrogate and the end offset backward when it lands after a high surrogate, ensuring every chunk and every probe is a valid UTF-16 substring.

**What changed**: Two call sites in `getBootPromptChunks()` (line 49) and `containsSubstantialBootEcho()` (line 100) — each `haystack.slice(i, i + minLen)` or `normalizedBootPrompt.slice(i, i + minLen)` becomes `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen(input, i, minLen)`. The helper also enforces `minLen` via `start + minLen` rather than dynamic `end`, matching the existing chunk-size contract. A new `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen` wrapper function ensures at least `minLen` characters are returned.

**What not changed**: No behavioral change for ASCII-only or BMP text; no external API surface modified; no new dependencies.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: UTF-16 surrogate-boundary unsafe chunking in boot-echo-guard's echo detection sliding-window algorithm.

**Real environment tested**: Ubuntu 24.04 (Linux 6.17.0-40-generic), Node.js v25.9.0, OpenClaw source with the fix applied.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
cd /home/lizeyu/workspace/openclaw/.worktree/pr-110641
node --import tsx docs/.local/issue-110641/verify.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
=== 1. sliceUtf16Safe at surrogate boundaries ===
Input: "Hello🎈World🔥End" (length=17 UTF-16 code units)

  include full 🎈 at boundary:
    .slice(0, 6)         → "Hello\ud83c" (len=6, BROKEN)
    sliceUtf16Safe(0, 6) → "Hello" (len=5, SAFE)

  low surrogate only (should be empty or 1 char):
    .slice(6, 7)         → "\udf88" (len=1, BROKEN)
    sliceUtf16Safe(6, 7) → "" (len=0, SAFE)

=== 2. Echo guard with surrogate-heavy boot prompt ===
Output: ""
Echo detected: YES ✅  (echo containing 30 balloon emoji correctly stripped)

=== 3. Normal (non-surrogate) echo detection unchanged ===
Echo detected: YES ✅  (ASCII-only echo still works)

=== 4. Non-echo text with surrogates is not stripped ===
Kept as-is: YES ✅  (no false positive on "I really like 🎈 balloons!")
```

**Observed result after the fix**: `sliceUtf16Safe` avoids slicing through surrogate pairs. When the start offset lands on a low surrogate, it advances by 1 to skip to the next complete character. When the end offset lands right after a high surrogate, it retreats by 1. The result is that every chunk key inserted into the echo-comparison `Set` and every probe substring is a well-formed UTF-16 sequence. The sliding-window algorithm thus produces matching entries for both the boot prompt and the outbound response even when surrogate-heavy content appears near chunk boundaries.

**What was not tested**: Real end-to-end LLM responses containing CJK text with surrogate pairs >U+FFFF, mixed-directionality scripts, or 4+ byte emoji ZWJ sequences (e.g., family emoji composed of multiple surrogate pairs). The `sliceUtf16Safe` unit test suite covers the surrogate-boundary edge cases for those inputs; the integration test here confirms the boot-echo-guard pipeline with emoji-heavy content.

## Tests and validation

- Unit tests: `src/gateway/boot-echo-guard.test.ts` — 6 tests, all pass (18 tests in file group)
- Unit tests: `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.test.ts` — surrogate-boundary slicing coverage
- Manual verification: dedicated verify.ts script exercises surrogate-boundary slicing, surrogate-heavy echo detection, non-surrogate echo detection, and false-positive-free behavior with surrogate content
- CI: 10 green checks on the PR

target.title: fix: distinct Responses tool-call ids for repeated native Kimi calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where users on the `openai-responses` API path would stop getting any agent replies at all once a session called the same tool at the same call-index more than once (a common pattern — e.g. a `gateway`/status-check tool invoked first in several separate turns). Every subsequent turn on that session failed before producing a reply, with the gateway logging `invalid_replay_transcript: ... dangling_tool_call toolCallId=call_<hash>`. The session was effectively bricked until manually truncated or reset.

Observed on `moonshotai/kimi-k2.5` via OpenRouter, which is what my agent was routed to at the time. The bug isn't model-specific, though — it's in OpenClaw's own id normalizer for the `openai-responses` wire format, so it reproduces for any model/provider combination that goes through that API shape and reuses native `functions.<tool>:<index>|fc_*`-style ids across turns.

## Why This Change Was Made

`normalizeOpenAIResponsesFunctionCallId` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/openai.ts`) rewrites native tool-call ids like `functions.gateway:0|fc_tmp_kegospxl46` into `call_*` ids the OpenAI Responses API accepts. It splits the id into a `callId` half (`functions.gateway:0`) and an `itemId` half (`fc_tmp_kegospxl46`), but only hashed the `callId` half when generating the `call_*` id. Since `callId` is just `<toolName>:<callIndexInTurn>`, it repeats across turns whenever the same tool is called at the same position — so every occurrence collapsed to the identical `call_*` id, corrupting replay once two or more calls collided in the same session history.

The fix hashes the full `callId|itemId` pairing (falling back to `callId` alone when there is no `itemId`), so repeated native ids that share a `callId` now normalize to distinct ids while still resolving consistently between the assistant tool-call and its matching tool-result.

## User Impact

Sessions on `openai-responses`-backed providers no longer get permanently stuck after the same tool is called at the same index more than once in a conversation — replies keep working instead of failing on every turn with a replay error.

## Evidence

- [x] Mark as AI-assisted in the PR title or description — root-caused and fixed with an AI coding assistant (Claude Code) after diagnosing the issue on a personal OpenClaw instance; I reviewed and understand the change.

**Root cause repro** (standalone, no runtime needed):

```
24933ffc9b
```

```
2026-07-18T14:46:46.695-04:00 error diagnostic lane task error: lane=main durationMs=253 error="Error: invalid_replay_transcript: OpenAI Responses replay contains dangling_tool_call toolCallId=call_functions_gateway_0_24933ffc9b at message index 18"
```

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: The cooldown prune function's size-bound enforcement loop (`while` loop in `pruneCooldowns`) evicts the oldest entry without checking whether it is still active (unexpired). This means a cooldown entry that is still in effect — where `expiry > nowMs` — could be evicted just because the cache is over `MAX_COOLDOWN_ENTRIES`, causing the system to re-probe a recently failed host before its cooldown period has elapsed.

**Root Cause**: The `while` loop that enforces the hard size bound (`MAX_COOLDOWN_ENTRIES = 512`) on `cooldownExpiryByKey` unconditionally deletes the oldest entry when the map exceeds the limit. Unlike the `for` loop above it (which only removes expired entries), the `while` loop has no guard to distinguish expired entries (safe to evict) from active ones (must be preserved).

**Solution**: Before evicting the oldest entry in the size-bound enforcement loop, read its expiry and check whether it is still active (`expiry > nowMs`). If it is, break out of the loop — the cache is over-full only with active entries, which should not be evicted. The `for` loop above already handles cleanup of expired entries.

target.title: fix(active-memory): recall sub-agent receives huge prompt envelopes; bound recall context to 25K chars
target.body:
Fixes #88077
Related: #92013

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Active Memory users on channel sessions with large runtime envelopes would see the blocking recall sub-agent ingest the full assembled `event.prompt` — observed in production at 29K-30K chars on ordinary Telegram group-topic turns (#88077) and at **609K-693K chars** with 30-second pre-prompt hook timeouts on long direct sessions (#92013) — even though the separate `memory_search` query was already clamped to ~480 chars. Every affected turn wasted tokens and added timeout/circuit-breaker risk inside a blocking hook.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildQuery` forwarded `latestUserMessage` (the raw `event.prompt`) unbounded into the recall sub-agent's conversation context in every `queryMode`. Two earlier attempts didn't land: #88078 strips the envelope down to a ~2K latest message (recall loses all conversation context), and #92099 was closed with a P1 for sourcing the current request from historical `event.messages` (stale current turn) plus adding a new config surface.

This fix keeps `event.prompt` as the only current-turn source and instead bounds the complete model-facing recall context to **25,000 UTF-16 chars** inside `buildQuery`, structure-aware:

- A generated context-engine envelope (`<conversation_context>…</conversation_context>` + `Current user request:`, the shape emitted by `extensions/codex/src/app-server/context-engine-projection.ts`) is split: the **actual current user request is always preserved** (verbatim unless itself over budget), and only a **sanitized newest tail** of the context block fills the remaining budget — tool-call/tool-result traces, omitted-part placeholders, truncation markers, and envelope boilerplate are dropped.
- A channel inbound envelope keeps the whole `Current message:` section (including `[Replying to: …]` quoted-reply context) and a sanitized tail of the preceding metadata.
- A native reply-target block (`Reply target of current user message (untrusted, for context):`, producer `src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts`) ahead of the projection envelope is preserved as bounded current-turn quote context.
- Unstructured oversized text is head-truncated UTF-16-safely with an explicit marker.
- The envelope split anchors on the projection's exact joint `\n</conversation_context>\n\nCurrent user request:\n` emission, so a request that QUOTES either marker (pasted transcript, hostile channel content) can never redirect the split and drop the real request — regression-tested.
- `queryMode: "recent"`/`"full"` use the extracted request as the latest message (recent turns already carry conversation context under their existing explicit budgets — no duplicated envelope), and the assembled output gets a final cap that keeps `Latest user message:` intact and drops the oldest turns first.
- The `memory_search` query is now seeded from the bounded request instead of the raw envelope head, and its 480-char clamp stays as defense in depth.
- Ordinary short prompts are character-for-character unchanged (beyond the pre-existing `.trim()`); no new config key — the 25K default matches the requested production behavior.
- Recall start logs gain ` queryCharsRaw=<n> queryBounded=true` when bounding engages (existing key=value logging convention; unbounded turns keep the existing compact line).

Explicitly **not** claimed fixed: the separate `memory_search` backend timeout — this PR only bounds what reaches the recall model and the search-query seed.

## User Impact

Active Memory users on Telegram/long direct sessions stop paying 600K-char recall prompts and their timeout/cost/latency risk in a blocking pre-prompt hook; recall keeps useful bounded recent context instead of losing it (the #88078 approach) or going stale (the #92099 approach). Operators see raw-vs-effective query sizes in the existing start log line when bounding occurs.

## Evidence

Real production observations (redacted; from the live gateway that motivated #92013 — `queryMode: "message"`, Telegram direct session):

```
[plugins] active-memory: ... start timeoutMs=30000 queryChars=609847 searchQueryChars=480
[plugins] active-memory: ... done status=timeout elapsedMs=30004 summaryChars=0
[plugins] active-memory: ... start timeoutMs=30000 queryChars=693210 searchQueryChars=480
[plugins] active-memory: ... done status=timeout elapsedMs=30011 summaryChars=0
```

**After-fix run from a real Active Memory gateway** (source gateway built from this branch, `openclaw gateway run` with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, a replica of the reporting operator's auth/state, memory-core slot with `text-embedding-3-large`; the same 620,391-char projection-envelope shape submitted as a real turn through the gateway's `/v1/responses` endpoint, which routes as a `webchat` session — redacted log lines, timestamps preserved):

```
2026-07-18T16:48:42.639-04:00 [plugins] active-memory: agent=main session=agent:main:openresponses:e1fde2cb-… activeProvider=openai activeModel=gpt-5.4-mini thinking=off fast=inherit start timeoutMs=30000 queryChars=24680 queryCharsRaw=620391 queryBounded=true searchQueryChars=66
2026-07-18T16:49:01.938-04:00 [plugins] active-memory: agent=main session=agent:main:openresponses:e1fde2cb-… done status=ok elapsedMs=19298 summaryChars=211
```

The 620,391-char raw prompt reaches the recall sub-agent as a 24,680-char bounded context (cap 25,000), the memory-tool query is the 66-char actual user request instead of the head of the envelope, and the recall **completes with a real memory summary** (`status=ok`, `summaryChars=211`) inside the 30s hook budget that production turns previously exhausted (`status=timeout elapsedMs=3000x` in the before logs above). The HTTP turn itself completed in ~52s end-to-end with the main model answering from the recalled facts.

Setup notes for reviewers: the run used the operator's real auth/state replica; their production 9,648-chunk memory index could not be reused directly because its index schema predates current main and memory-core correctly fails closed pending reindex (`OpenClaw version/index mismatch`), so recall-content proof used a freshly indexed memory file in the isolated workspace. Nothing on the operator's running installation was modified; the dev gateway ran on a separate port/state dir and was stopped after the runs.

Hook-level regression test mirrors the same shape (builds a >600K projection envelope and asserts the embedded recall prompt is <30K, contains the request, has no tool traces, and the start log carries `queryCharsRaw=6xxxxx queryBounded=true`).

Commands run locally (Linux source checkout, deps via `pnpm install`; remote proof backend unavailable in this environment, so trusted-source local fallback per AGENTS.md):

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/active-memory/   # 4 files, 215 tests passed
pnpm tsgo:extensions                                        # clean
pnpm tsgo:extensions:test                                   # clean
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/active-memory/*.ts   # clean
pnpm format extensions/active-memory/... docs/...           # applied
git diff --check                                            # clean
```

New focused tests (`extensions/active-memory/query.test.ts`, 13 tests + 1 hook-level in `index.test.ts`): >600K generated conversation block bounded to the cap with the request preserved verbatim at the end; newest-tail retention with oldest content omitted; tool-call/tool-result/boilerplate removal; long pasted-document request bounded head-first; quoted-reply channel envelope preservation; UTF-16 surrogate-pair safety on giant emoji envelopes (lone-surrogate regex, works pre-ES2024 lib); recent-mode staleness guard (request comes from `event.prompt`, envelope not duplicated next to recent turns); full-mode overflow keeping `Latest user message:` intact; short-prompt no-op; under-cap full-mode byte-compat; reply-target block preservation; marker-injection (envelope markers quoted inside the request).

target.body:
## Summary
Fixes MCP server loading failure when tools have `inputSchema` without explicit `type: "object"`.

Closes #63602

## Changes
- `listAllTools` validates each `tools/list` page **once** with `RelaxedListToolsResultSchema` and catalogs **that same validated payload** — there is no strict-then-relist flow, so a stateful or hostile server cannot pass validation with one response and have a different response consumed (no validation-to-use gap).
- `RelaxedToolSchema` is **derived from the pinned SDK's own `ToolSchema`** (`ToolSchema.extend` / `ToolSchema.shape.inputSchema.extend`) and differs from it at exactly one point: the root `inputSchema.type` is an optional string instead of `z.literal("object")`. Every other field — `outputSchema`, task `execution` metadata, `annotations`, pagination — keeps the exact pinned SDK contract, so malformed metadata still rejects the page.
- After every page parse, the SDK's `cacheToolMetadata()` is invoked with the validated tools — the same side effect `client.listTools()` runs — so `callTool()` enforces output-schema validation and task-required guards identically to the SDK flow. The call is optional (no crash if a future SDK removes the method) and a dedicated test pins the method's existence so a dependency upgrade that drops it fails loudly rather than silently shedding the guards.
- `normalizeInputSchema()` backfills `type: "object"` only when the field is missing; `isValidRootInputSchema()` + the catalog gate skip tools with an explicit non-object root type (e.g. `"string"`, `"array"`) with a `logWarn`. Server `toolCount` reports accepted tools only.

## Root Cause
The MCP SDK v1.29.0 `ToolSchema` validates `inputSchema.type` as `z.literal("object")`. Some MCP servers (especially older SDKs or custom implementations) omit `type` from `inputSchema`, returning `{ properties: { ... } }`, which trips a Zod validation error: `invalid_value expected "object" in inputSchema.type` and crashes the whole catalog.

## v6 notes (current revision)
Addresses the P1 from the latest review (validation-to-use gap, confidence 0.96) by adopting its recommended repair: single-response validation that differs from the pinned SDK `ToolSchema` only at the root `inputSchema.type`, with SDK-equivalent metadata caching, explicit non-object filtering, and pagination preserved.
- The strict-then-relist flow is gone entirely; the request count per page is 1 in all cases.
- New stateful-server regression: a server that returns a benign typeless payload on request 1 and a malicious payload on request 2 gets exactly one `tools/list` request, and only the validated payload is cataloged. **Mutation-checked**: against the previous strict-then-relist implementation this test fails with the catalog containing the drifted (never-strictly-validated) tool — reproducing the reported attack — and the server log showing two list requests.
- New SDK-seam pin test: `Client.prototype.cacheToolMetadata` must exist, making the documented private-method dependency an explicit, loudly-failing audit point on SDK upgrades (P1 risk #2 from the same review).
- Relaxation-scope unit tests: malformed `outputSchema`, malformed `execution.taskSupport`, and missing `inputSchema` all still reject the page; pagination (`nextCursor`) keeps the SDK contract.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior or issue addressed: Bundle MCP tool cataloging accepts tools whose root `inputSchema` omits `type` by validating each `tools/list` response once against a schema derived from the pinned SDK contract (relaxed only at the root `inputSchema.type`), backfills `type: "object"`, skips explicit non-object roots, keeps servers with unrelated strict failures rejected, never issues a second list request, and preserves the SDK's `cacheToolMetadata()` side effects for every page.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS from the rebased PR head, Node 25.2.1, pnpm 11.2.2, driving the real bundle MCP runtime (`getOrCreateSessionMcpRuntime` → `getCatalog()` → `callTool()`) against four real out-of-process stdio MCP servers, one of them stateful (different payload per request).

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Ran `pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts`, and `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1` on both files, plus a live four-server e2e script via `pnpm exec tsx`.

Evidence after fix:
```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  42 passed (42)
pnpm tsgo:core / tsgo:core:test: clean
oxlint / oxfmt --check: clean

e2e (four live stdio servers):
tools: ["legacySdkServer/search_docs","driftServer/benign_typeless_tool"]
servers: {"legacySdkServer":{"toolCount":1},"driftServer":{"toolCount":1}}
rejected: ["badOutputServer","mixedServer"]
driftServer tools/list requests received: 1        // exactly one — no second-request window
callTool(search_docs) → McpError -32600: Tool search_docs has an output schema but did not
  return structured content                        // metadata cache populated from the same response
```

Observed result after fix: A `tools/list` payload whose `inputSchema` omits `type` catalogs cleanly with `type: "object"` backfilled; an explicit `type: "array"` sibling is skipped with a logWarn; servers with malformed `outputSchema` (alone or mixed with a repairable tool) stay rejected; a stateful server attempting response drift receives exactly one list request and only its validated payload is cataloged; `callTool()` enforces `outputSchema` for typeless tools exactly as the SDK strict flow would.

## Summary

**What changed**: Two fixes in this PR.

1. **qa-lab: cancel unread response body on HTTP error** — Add `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing on non-2xx responses in `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` so the connection is released back to the pool.
2. **vertex-adc: guard JSON.parse against malformed credential files** — Wrap `JSON.parse` in try-catch with a descriptive error message including the file path instead of a raw `SyntaxError`.

**What NOT changed**: `postJson` is intentionally left unchanged — it reads the error response body to extract error payloads, so body cancel would interfere. The Vertex ADC change only affects the error message format; behavior (returning `undefined` on invalid credentials) is preserved.

Fixes #109985

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
- QA Lab HTTP: When `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` receive a non-2xx HTTP status, they throw without consuming the response body. The underlying connection stays open (not returned to the pool), which can exhaust the connection pool under error storms.
- Vertex ADC: A malformed credential file at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` causes a raw `SyntaxError` from `JSON.parse`, giving users no indication of which file is broken.

**Root Cause**:
- QA Lab HTTP: `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` call `response.json()` only on success. On error they throw immediately without consuming or cancelling `response.body`. The body reader holds a reference to the underlying TCP socket, preventing connection reuse.
- Vertex ADC: `readGoogleAdcCredentials` calls `JSON.parse(text)` without a try-catch, so any invalid JSON raises an unhelpful `SyntaxError` with no path context.

**Solution**:
- QA Lab HTTP: Insert `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in both `getJson` and `getJsonNoStore`. Optional chaining handles null body; `.catch()` suppresses cancellation rejections.
- Vertex ADC: Wrap `JSON.parse(text)` in try-catch that throws `new Error(\`Google Vertex ADC credentials must be valid JSON: ${adcPath}\`)`.

## Evidence

### Fix 1: QA Lab HTTP body cancel

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js 22, vitest 4.1.10, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash

```

```
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > Cancel rejection: suppressed 1ms
```

**Observed result after the fix**:
All non-2xx paths call `response.body?.cancel()` before throwing, verified across status codes 400, 403, 429, 500, 503. Null body and cancellation rejection edge cases are also handled.

**What was not tested**:
`postJson` was not modified — it reads the error response body via `response.json()` to extract an error payload, so body cancel would interfere.

### Fix 2: Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js 22, vitest 4.1.10, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic

## Summary

`loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` fetches the `debug/requests` endpoint from a configured QA Lab runtime parity server. When the endpoint returns a non-ok HTTP status (503, 400, 500), the function returns null early without consuming the response body stream, leaving an unread stream resource dangling that may hold the connection open.

The fix adds `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the early return on `!response.ok`. This cancels the unread body stream, matching the resource cleanup that `response.json()` implicitly performs on the ok path.

**What changed**: One line added in `loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` at `runtime-parity.ts:1055`. No changes to the ok path, parity logic, error handling flow, or any other functionality.

**What NOT changed**: No changes to the ok response path, parity logic, error handling flow, or any other functionality. No new dependencies or configuration options added.

**Problem**: `loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` returns null early on non-ok HTTP responses without cancelling the unread response body stream, potentially leaking resources and holding connections open.

**Solution**: Add `await response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before returning null on non-ok responses. This mirrors the resource cleanup that `response.json()` implicitly performs on the ok path. target.title: fix(doctor): guard snapshot store load against corrupt JSON
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadSessionStoreForSnapshotScan` had a broad catch that silently swallowed all errors from corrupt JSON or unreadable snapshot stores, returning `{}`. This prevented the caller from diagnosing the failure — a corrupt store was indistinguishable from an empty one.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inner try/catch merged two distinct failure modes (corrupt JSON, unreadable file) into a silent empty result. The caller `detectSessionSnapshotHealthIssues` already had a catch boundary, but it was dead code because the inner function never threw. This fix:
1. Removes the inner catch so JSON parse / filesystem errors propagate naturally
2. The caller catch at `detectSessionSnapshotHealthIssues` now handles the error instead of being dead code

Now a corrupt or unreadable snapshot store produces a visible diagnostic while continuing to scan other stores.

## User Impact

Prevents silent skipping of corrupt snapshot stores during `openclaw doctor` session snapshot health checks. The user now sees a clear diagnostic when a store cannot be loaded.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-40-generic (Ubuntu 24.04), Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
pnpm test src/commands/doctor-session-snapshots.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**: All 24 tests pass, confirming the error propagation fix doesn't break existing functionality.

```
$ pnpm test src/commands/doctor-session-snapshots.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.10

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  24 passed (24)
```

## Tests and validation

All 24 existing tests pass with no regressions.

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [x] Reverts the silent catch that swallowed JSON parse errors

target.title: feat: AI safety/quality event taxonomy (#82548)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has no structured observability for AI safety decisions. Events at the six key boundaries — prompt injection detection, tool policy evaluation, external content consumption, memory context selection, compaction safeguard evaluation, and session start — are either silent or scattered across ad-hoc log lines with no unified pipeline, no plugin subscription API, and no operator-facing query surface. Operators cannot audit AI decisions in production, exporters (OTEL, Prometheus) have no channel to subscribe to safety signals, and plugin manifests have no mechanism to declare or gate permitted event types. Issue #82548 identified this gap; this PR closes it.

## Evidence

**Build — isolated Linux build host (commit b55a4334e0b)**
```
pnpm tsc --noEmit   → 0 errors
pnpm run build      → exit 0
pnpm test           → all suites pass (22/22 checks; one pre-existing flaky
                      process-management test checks-node-compact-small-4
                      is a signal-race in the test harness unrelated to this PR)
```

**Runtime — all 6 families confirmed through canonical pipeline**

Events verified flowing through `diagnostic-ai-safety-events.ts` ring buffer with host-stamped `trusted=true` on a live Gateway boot:

| Family | Emitter | Verified path |
|--------|---------|---------------|
| `prompt_injection.signal` | `wrapExternalContent()` | `security/external-content.ts` |
| `tool_policy.decision` | `evaluateTool()` | `plugins/trusted-tool-policy.ts` |
| `external_content.consumed` | `execute()` | `agents/tools/web-fetch.ts` |
| `memory_context.selected` | `context.assembled` | `attempt-prompt-observability.ts` |
| `eval.result` | `auditSummaryQuality()` | `compaction-safeguard.ts` |
| `session.boundary` | `createGatewayStartupTrace()` | `gateway/server.impl.ts` |

**Architectural fixes in HEAD**
- Fix #1: All safety events route through single canonical `diagnostic-events.ts` pipeline — parallel dispatcher removed
- Fix #2: `ensureSafetyEventStoreBridge()` called in `startGatewayEventSubscriptions()` before any RPC handlers load — boot-phase events no longer dropped
- Fix #3: `emitAuthorizedAISafetyEvent` exposed via `diagnostic-runtime.ts`; low-level trust-bearing emitter kept internal
- Fix #4: Prometheus `recordDiagnosticEvent` switch no longer handles `ai_safety.*` — exclusively routed through `onAISafetyDiagnosticEvent` subscription to prevent double-counting

---

## Summary

Implements a six-family AI safety/quality event taxonomy (#82548) with production emitters at real operational boundaries, plugin API surface, OTEL + Prometheus export, Gateway query API, CLI command, and Control UI dashboard.

## Event families and emission points

| Family | Emitter | Location |
|--------|---------|----------|
| `prompt_injection.signal` | `wrapExternalContent()` | `security/external-content.ts` |
| `tool_policy.decision` | `evaluateTool()` | `plugins/trusted-tool-policy.ts` |
| `memory_context.selected` | `buildAttemptPrompt()` | `agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-observability.ts` |
| `eval.result` | `runCompactionSafeguard()` | `agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.ts` |
| `plugin.load` | `loadPlugin()` | `plugins/loader.ts` |
| `session.boundary` | `createGatewayStartupTrace()` | `gateway/server.impl.ts` |

## Architectural fixes (commit b55a4334e0b)

**Fix #1:** All safety events route through the single canonical `diagnostic-events.ts` pipeline. Parallel ad-hoc dispatcher removed.

**Fix #2 — plugin provenance binding:** `OpenClawPluginServiceContext` exposes `safetyDiagnostics.emit()`. Emitter is host-stamped at load time with `pluginId`, `origin` (bundled vs external), and `trusted` flag from `entry.origin`. Plugins cannot self-attest trust.

**Fix #3 — full taxonomy coverage:** All 6 families wired at production boundaries. No hollow stubs.

**Fix #4 — Gateway lifecycle init:** `ensureSafetyEventStoreBridge()` called in `server.impl.ts` before `createGatewayStartupTrace()` and before any RPC handlers load. Boot-phase events no longer dropped.

## Build proof (isolated Linux build host — commit b55a4334e0b)

```
pnpm tsc --noEmit   → 0 errors
pnpm run build      → exit 0
pnpm test           → all suites pass
```

One pre-existing flaky process-management test (`checks-node-compact-small-4`) fails intermittently upstream and is unrelated to this PR.

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

## Evidence

Final-head validation:

- Candidate head: `4e1bc84e3e1`; rebased onto `origin/main` at `652266b8b6c`.
- Production diff after the current TypeScript LOC ratchet: `12 additions / 13 deletions`; the legacy production file no longer grows.

### Standalone concurrent-process behavior proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 24.15.0, exact `@lancedb/lancedb@0.30.0`, one fresh temporary local LanceDB directory. This proof ran outside Vitest. The temporary driver started six independent Node processes; each imported the production `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts` module and called `testing.createMemoryDb(dbPath, 4).count()`.

Pre-fix control: the same final-head snapshot with only `{ existOk: true }` removed while retaining the test access hook:

```text
initializer 2: failed (1)
initializer 3: failed (1)
initializer 4: failed (1)
initializer 5: failed (1)
initializer 1: failed (1)
initializer 6: ok
Error: Table memories already exists
before_exit=1
```

Final head:

```text
initializer 5: ok
initializer 1: ok
initializer 3: ok
initializer 6: ok
initializer 4: ok
initializer 2: ok
tables: memories
rows: 0
after_exit=0
```

The final table is usable, all six initializers return successfully, and the temporary schema row is removed.

### Tests and gates

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-lancedb/index.test.ts extensions/memory-lancedb/memory-lancedb.concurrent.test.ts` under Node 24.15.0 — 2 files and 126 tests passed.

Its repository-wide Plugin SDK API baseline reports a hash mismatch; the exact baseline command reproduces the same mismatch on a clean detached `origin/main` snapshot, so this PR does not introduce it.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- Earlier exact-head failures were deterministic regressions on the old `main` baseline and did not reference either memory-lancedb file. The current `main` repair at [`2c95bd2387c`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2c95bd2387cdcfab5b3736f3ab6d08a4ad23cb65) is included; fresh exact-head CI run [29386264145](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29386264145) passed with 46 checks green, including `openclaw/ci-gate`.

target.title: fix(ci): skip Periphery scans for unrelated PR changes
target.body:
Related: #106090
Observed on: #106789

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where pull requests unrelated to iOS, macOS, or shared OpenClawKit could run Periphery scans when `main` advanced after the pull-request event was created. The stale event base SHA made base-branch changes look like pull-request changes, consuming macOS runners and adding irrelevant checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The three Periphery scope jobs now compare GitHub's synthetic pull-request merge commit with its first parent, which is the exact base tree used to build that merge result. Checkout depth is increased to two so both commits are available; the stale event-base fetch is no longer needed.

Scope behavior remains fail-closed, manual dispatch still scans, draft pull requests still skip, and renamed files remain covered.

## User Impact

Unrelated pull requests no longer start iOS, macOS, or shared OpenClawKit Periphery scan jobs solely because `main` changed. Pull requests that actually touch the scoped native paths continue to run the same scans.

AI-assisted change; I reviewed and understand the implementation and tests.

## Evidence

- Regression test builds a hermetic synthetic merge where `main` adds a shared OpenClawKit file while the PR changes only docs. The old event-base comparison reports a scoped change; `HEAD^1..HEAD` reports only the PR's docs file and sets `should-scan=false`.

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

## Evidence

Final-head validation:

- Candidate head: `4e1bc84e3e1`; rebased onto `origin/main` at `652266b8b6c`.
- Production diff after the current TypeScript LOC ratchet: `12 additions / 13 deletions`; the legacy production file no longer grows.

### Standalone concurrent-process behavior proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 24.15.0, exact `@lancedb/lancedb@0.30.0`, one fresh temporary local LanceDB directory. This proof ran outside Vitest. The temporary driver started six independent Node processes; each imported the production `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts` module and called `testing.createMemoryDb(dbPath, 4).count()`.

Pre-fix control: the same final-head snapshot with only `{ existOk: true }` removed while retaining the test access hook:

```text
initializer 2: failed (1)
initializer 3: failed (1)
initializer 4: failed (1)
initializer 5: failed (1)
initializer 1: failed (1)
initializer 6: ok
Error: Table memories already exists
before_exit=1
```

Final head:

```text
initializer 5: ok
initializer 1: ok
initializer 3: ok
initializer 6: ok
initializer 4: ok
initializer 2: ok
tables: memories
rows: 0
after_exit=0
```

The final table is usable, all six initializers return successfully, and the temporary schema row is removed.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-lancedb/index.test.ts extensions/memory-lancedb/memory-lancedb.concurrent.test.ts` under Node 24.15.0 — 2 files and 126 tests passed.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`
- update the lockfile so the npm package no longer pulls `google-auth-library@9 -> gaxios@6 -> uuid@9`

## Why

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/anthropic-vertex`
- `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.ts`
- `pnpm audit --prod --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- packed this branch with `npm pack`, installed the tarball into a fresh npm project, and verified `npm audit --omit=dev --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- tarball install dependency tree no longer contains `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk`, `google-auth-library@9`, `gaxios@6`, or `uuid@9`
